lessons.title: The tenant boundary
outcomes: Every later object, from a dial plan to a recorder, lives in one tenant. Pairing an SBC in the wrong tenant is a different phone system.

lessons.title: Entra ID accounts voice will use
outcomes: Licenses and policies attach to Entra objects. A queue that nobody can find in the directory cannot be licensed.

lessons.title: Roles that can change voice
outcomes: Global Administrator is not a voice habit. The role you use decides what an audit can prove later.

lessons.title: The admin-center map
outcomes: Voice objects are split across the Teams admin center, the Microsoft 365 admin center, and PowerShell. Hunting in one pane wastes the outage.

lessons.title: Exchange and Cloud Voicemail
outcomes: Voicemail is an Exchange dependency. A clean SBC trace can still mean a lost message.

lessons.title: What homed online means
outcomes: A license on a user who is still homed on a legacy registrar will not produce Direct Routing calls.

lessons.title: The license stack
outcomes: The wrong SKU looks like a routing bug and survives every SBC reboot.

lessons.title: Calling Plan flavors
outcomes: Domestic, international, and pay-as-you-go are different purchases. The country list is part of the product.

lessons.title: Teams Premium is not PSTN
outcomes: Premium is a meeting add-on. Treating it as the phone license produces a design that cannot dial.

lessons.title: Resource account licenses
outcomes: Attendants and queues fail closed when the resource account has the wrong SKU, or had the right SKU removed in two steps.

lessons.title: Rooms, common area, and shared calling
outcomes: Devices and shared numbers have their own license sentences. Copying a user bundle onto a hallway phone wastes money and still may not work.

lessons.title: A license set you can defend
outcomes: Interviews and design reviews both ask for the set, not a brand name.

lessons.title: The module and the session
outcomes: The shell is how you read effective policy and how you assign compliance recording. The portal will not show you every object.

lessons.title: Objects you will actually get
outcomes: Voice routing is a handful of objects. If you can draw them, the cmdlets are spelling.

lessons.title: Grant, set, and new
outcomes: New creates, set changes, grant assigns. Mixing them up is how a policy is edited and never reaches the user.

lessons.title: Reading a user before you change one
outcomes: The pilot user is often not the user you think. Group assignment hides the policy you just edited.

lessons.title: When the portal and the shell disagree
outcomes: The toast is not the directory. The directory is what the next call will use.

lessons.title: Safety on a lab tenant
outcomes: Certificate and routing experiments belong where a mistake cannot take the company’s numbers away.

lessons.title: Shortest path, no media proxy
outcomes: Teams media hates hairpins and proxies. Bandwidth is the expensive way to hide a bad path.

lessons.title: The port and DSCP table
outcomes: This table is the QoS interview. It is also the ACL.

lessons.title: VPN and the split tunnel
outcomes: A full-tunnel VPN adds delay and hides the office subnet from emergency location and from CQD.

lessons.title: Bandwidth you can calculate
outcomes: 64 kbit/s is the payload. The link carries headers too.

lessons.title: Proving the mark survived
outcomes: A client policy that the WAN undoes is not QoS.

lessons.title: ExpressRoute is not the requirement
outcomes: A private circuit is a purchasing choice. It is not the Teams network requirement.

lessons.title: Four ways to reach the PSTN
outcomes: The connectivity option decides who operates the carrier, who you call at 2 a.m., and which license you buy.

lessons.title: Calling Plans in practice
outcomes: This is the option with the least SBC work and the least control.

lessons.title: Operator Connect
outcomes: You keep a carrier relationship without operating the SBC.

lessons.title: Teams Phone Mobile
outcomes: The SIM number and the Teams number are the same number. That is a gift for frontline staff and a trap for a reception queue.

lessons.title: Direct Routing
outcomes: This is the option when you still own trunks, a PBX, analog devices, or a contact-center SBC.

lessons.title: Mixing them in one tenant
outcomes: The plan page’s own example puts knowledge workers on Operator Connect, frontline on Teams Phone Mobile, contact centers on Direct Routing, and a small office on Calling Plans.

lessons.title: Normalize, then route
outcomes: Routes match the number after the dial plan. A perfect route that expects E.164 will never see a local habit.

lessons.title: Dial plans and first match
outcomes: A branch that dials differently needs its own plan. Editing the global plan does not change a user who has a more specific one.

lessons.title: PSTN usages are the permission
outcomes: A route without a usage on the user’s policy is invisible. A usage on the wrong policy is an international bill.

lessons.title: Voice routes and gateways
outcomes: The route is a regular expression plus an ordered list of SBCs. CUCM wildcards will not work here.

lessons.title: A London worked example
outcomes: One concrete walk is worth a page of definitions.

lessons.title: Islands mode and other hard stops
outcomes: Some failures are not routing tweaks. They are unsupported states.

lessons.title: Resource accounts for voice apps
outcomes: The attendant and the queue are not callable until an account represents them.

lessons.title: Auto attendant design
outcomes: The published company number is usually this object. A sloppy menu is a public defect.

lessons.title: Queue routing methods
outcomes: Attendant, serial, round robin, and longest idle are different promises to the people answering.

lessons.title: Timeout, overflow, and outbound funding
outcomes: A queue without overflow is a waiting room with a locked door.

lessons.title: Nested voice apps
outcomes: Real companies are a tree: one attendant, a few queues, an overflow attendant. The tree needs a picture.

lessons.title: Numbers on voice apps
outcomes: The number’s owner decides whether the company keeps it when a human leaves.

lessons.title: Emergency calling is a design gate
outcomes: A phone system that cannot reach emergency services is not ready, even if every other demo looks good.

lessons.title: Dynamic location
outcomes: A laptop moves. The address you shouted at install time does not.

lessons.title: Calling Plans versus Direct Routing emergency
outcomes: The client is Teams in both designs. The carrier is not.

lessons.title: Location-based routing
outcomes: Some countries treat toll bypass as a regulatory problem. Location-based routing is the Teams control.

lessons.title: Survivable Branch Appliance
outcomes: A WAN cut should not remove the ability to place a local PSTN call, including emergency.

lessons.title: Notification and the test call
outcomes: Responders at the wrong door, and a test that called the real emergency service, are both failures.

lessons.title: Certified phones
outcomes: A bargain SIP phone is not a Teams client. The certified list is the product boundary.

lessons.title: Teams Rooms
outcomes: A room account with a user license and a strict Conditional Access policy is a dark screen at the start of a meeting.

lessons.title: SIP Gateway and analog
outcomes: Elevators, door phones, and fax machines do not run the Teams client.

lessons.title: Media bypass
outcomes: Bypass changes where RTP flows. It does not change where SIP flows.

lessons.title: Local media optimization
outcomes: A branch SBC with one public interface can still hairpin local users out and back.

lessons.title: Common area phones, again, as devices
outcomes: The license sentence and the device sentence meet at the hallway.

lessons.title: What certification buys you
outcomes: Microsoft supports Direct Routing on certified SBCs. Everything else can be refused.

lessons.title: AudioCodes pattern
outcomes: Mediant SBCs are common in Teams designs. The pattern is still the shared gate, plus their guide.

lessons.title: Ribbon pattern
outcomes: Ribbon Core and software editions differ. The brand is not the release.

lessons.title: Oracle Communications SBC
outcomes: Oracle’s session border controller is a Direct Routing option only on the releases Microsoft lists.

lessons.title: Cisco CUBE for Teams
outcomes: CUBE is the usual bridge when CUCM is still in the building. It is still an SBC.

lessons.title: The support boundary
outcomes: Knowing who you call is part of the design.

lessons.title: The certificate profile
outcomes: SIP never starts if TLS fails. Dial-plan debates can wait.

lessons.title: Names, wildcards, and the paired FQDN
outcomes: A certificate can be valid and still be the wrong name.

lessons.title: Three SIP proxies and failover
outcomes: The service tells the SBC which proxy is nearest and fails between them. Your firewall has to allow all of them.

lessons.title: SIP OPTIONS
outcomes: OPTIONS are how Teams decides the trunk is willing. A dial plan cannot heal a trunk that does not answer.

lessons.title: Codecs and SRTP
outcomes: An empty codec list is a 488. Missing media ports is silence after a 200.

lessons.title: Failover you can rehearse
outcomes: The outage should not be the first test of the second proxy or the second SBC.

lessons.title: One hypothesis
outcomes: Bundled changes teach nothing and make rollback impossible.

lessons.title: Reading a ladder
outcomes: The response code is the branch. A story without codes is not a diagnosis.

lessons.title: Call Analytics
outcomes: One user, one call. That is the scope of this tool.

lessons.title: Call Quality Dashboard
outcomes: CQD is how you see a subnet. It is only as honest as the building map.

lessons.title: Trunk health
outcomes: A down trunk is not a dial-plan problem.

lessons.title: A fault catalog
outcomes: Naming the fault is the skill. The tools are how you prove the name.

lessons.title: Customer Service and Contact Center
outcomes: Dynamics 365 Contact Center is Microsoft’s CCaaS. Customer Service is not automatically that product.

lessons.title: Channels
outcomes: AB-250 weights channel implementation at about 30 to 35 percent, the largest published slice.

lessons.title: Unified routing
outcomes: Work items do not magically find experts. Classification and capacity do that, or fail to.

lessons.title: Representative experience and Copilot
outcomes: The person answering needs a console, a role, and assistance that quotes sources you trust.

lessons.title: Voice on ACS
outcomes: The contact-center voice channel is not a Teams call queue with a different logo.

lessons.title: The AB-250 map
outcomes: The published weights tell you where to spend the week.

lessons.title: Connect, Extend, and Unify
outcomes: The model decides the media path and the licenses. The sales adjective does not.

lessons.title: Teams Phone extensibility
outcomes: It is how a contact center uses the Teams Phone you already paid for, instead of a second PBX.

lessons.title: CUCM and CUBE
outcomes: Most Teams migrations in a Cisco estate are a dual-run, not a weekend miracle.

lessons.title: Webex calling interop
outcomes: A split estate needs a voice bridge. Chat federation is a different project.

lessons.title: UCCE during a move
outcomes: Contact-center agents and knowledge workers should not be forced through the same weekend.

lessons.title: Genesys and Amazon Connect
outcomes: Both appear in real estates. Neither is ‘a Microsoft feature’ you can assume.

lessons.title: Calling SDK versus Call Automation
outcomes: One is a person in a browser. The other is your service answering the call.

lessons.title: Teams interop from ACS
outcomes: A bot that can dial the PSTN and cannot reach a Teams expert is half an IVR.

lessons.title: An IVR as events
outcomes: The call is a sequence of events. If you cannot name them, you cannot debug them.

lessons.title: Azure AI Speech
outcomes: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech are services with their own language, voice, and approval rules.

lessons.title: Copilot Studio voice
outcomes: The agent people mean is often a Copilot Studio bot on the contact-center voice channel.

lessons.title: Foundry, and what not to invent
outcomes: Azure AI Foundry is where you evaluate a model. It does not route PSTN, and it used to be called Azure AI Studio.

lessons.title: MS-700 on 14 October 2026
outcomes: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement.

lessons.title: MB-280, AB-210, and AB-250
outcomes: These three numbers get swapped in job posts. Only one of them is the contact-center exam.

lessons.title: AZ-900 and SC-900
outcomes: Fundamentals help with Azure and identity vocabulary. They do not make you a voice engineer.

lessons.title: Learning paths that match the job
outcomes: A random trail of modules will not assemble a dial plan in your head.

lessons.title: The status board
outcomes: Dates are the part that makes a certification answer true or false.

lessons.title: How to use the readiness map
outcomes: A self-rating is useful only if a low score points at a lesson.

lessons.title: Voice is not a closed box
outcomes: The call is not finished when it rings. Recording, staffing, location, analytics, CRM, and agents are part of the same job.

lessons.title: How to use the glossary
outcomes: The glossary is the shared language for the map. Interviews punish fuzzy words.

lessons.title: The mind map
outcomes: A picture of the estate stops you from buying a second phone system by accident.

lessons.title: Compliance recording and quality management
outcomes: Regulated desks need a recorder the user cannot stop. Convenience recording is not that recorder.

lessons.title: Workforce management
outcomes: A queue without a staffing model is a guess. Teams user reports will not staff next Tuesday.

lessons.title: E911 as a system of record
outcomes: Location is data you operate, shared with routing and with quality maps.

lessons.title: Analytics and Power BI
outcomes: A dashboard is a view. Call Analytics, CQD, and contact-center analytics are different grains of truth.

lessons.title: CRM and screen pop
outcomes: The case is where the business remembers the call. Teams will not open Dynamics for an ordinary PSTN call by itself.

lessons.title: AI agents beside the queue
outcomes: A bot is a front door with a failure mode, not a headcount reduction you can assume.

lessons.title: Integration maps
outcomes: A goal implies a set of systems. Naming them prevents a tool from being asked to do a job it does not have.

lessons.title: Cross-platform bridges
outcomes: CUCM, Webex, UCCE, Genesys, and Amazon Connect all show up next to Teams. The bridge is an SBC and a rule, not a slogan.

lessons.title: Future-integration hooks
outcomes: A seam you name now is cheap. A rewrite after go-live is not. These hooks use products that exist today.

lessons.title: Configuring an ecosystem change
outcomes: A voice change that ignores the sisters will pass a test call and fail the business.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting across a vendor boundary
outcomes: The fault is usually on one side of a boundary. The argument is usually on both.

lessons.title: What CTI names
outcomes: The name is older than any of the products in this track. The vendor page still has to say what the product actually does.

lessons.title: The Dynamics voice channel
outcomes: The voice channel is the Dynamics page that says where PSTN calling lives, and which app the representative uses.

lessons.title: Teams Phone into the voice channel
outcomes: A Teams number can be the PSTN path. The page that allows it also limits which Calling Plan numbers qualify.

lessons.title: The resource account and the number
outcomes: The number does not appear in Dynamics until the resource account exists and someone runs Sync from Teams.

lessons.title: Salesforce Voice and Partner Contact Center
outcomes: The old name is still in product screens. The pages opened for this room say what the current name is.

lessons.title: Amazon Connect and partner telephony
outcomes: The help page does not collapse the telephony models into one setup path.

lessons.title: The call-to-record seam
outcomes: The bridge fails when the call and the CRM record do not share an identifier you stored.

lessons.title: A comparison with no winner
outcomes: A comparison is a set of sentences you can point at. A ranking is a sentence these pages do not contain.

lessons.title: What the Microsoft pages name
outcomes: Microsoft publishes more than one voice path. The page you cite has to be the path you mean.

lessons.title: Amazon Connect Customer
outcomes: The admin guide opened for this room uses a current product name that is not the old title.

lessons.title: CCAI Platform and the GECX rename
outcomes: The docs page and the legal change log do not print the same product title. Both were opened.

lessons.title: Documented differences only
outcomes: A table is safe when every cell comes from a page you can reopen.

lessons.title: What these pages do not decide
outcomes: The honest end of a comparison is the list of questions the opened pages do not answer.

lessons.title: Classification, then assignment
outcomes: Unified routing is two stages. Mixing them makes the wrong control look broken.

lessons.title: Voice workstreams and voice queues
outcomes: A voice workstream will not offer pick mode. The page says push only, and the choice cannot be edited later.

lessons.title: Highest capacity, round robin, least active
outcomes: The assignment method is a choice on the queue. The page defines three out-of-the-box methods this room can repeat.

lessons.title: Forecast, capacity, and schedule
outcomes: Workforce management in this stack starts as a forecast of volume and handle time. It is not a Teams calling policy.

lessons.title: Indicators and guardrails
outcomes: A quality indicator produces a score. A guardrail produces a violation. The page treats them as different objects.

lessons.title: Two recording controls
outcomes: Dynamics can play a recording announcement on the voice channel. Teams compliance recording is a separate policy.

lessons.title: Which control failed
outcomes: Routing, forecasting, and quality fail in different places. The first control you change should be the one the evidence names.
